title: Larkin's band, Cedric Haywood and Wild Bill Davis
summary: Back with Milton Larkin, Cobb describes a battle of music at the Eldorado Ballroom after which Wild Bill Davis joined, and how Davis took up guitar to stay on the stand.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: But let's get back now to Milt Larkin -- that's where we left.
Now you said your biggest influence was Joe Thomas.

All right, we've talked about Joe Thomas, we talked about Milt Larkin. When I got with Milton Larkin, we had a band that we billed with Milton supervising the situation -- he's a good organizer, a good businessman, and

was a good leader. Cedric Haywood was with that band, and then eventually we had a battle of music at the Eldorado Ballroom, the Wyler Wylie Collegiates came down and then that band had Wild Bill Davis on his senior year, but he was just Bill Davis then.
And he came down and joined us. He asked Milton; he talked to Milton about joining our band because he liked it, and Bill stayed with us two years. Bill Davis.
No, he was playing guitar, wasn't he?

Well, he was playing piano, but what made him go get a guitar, because Cedric played the piano, and they had to alternate, and Bill wanted to be on the stand staff, so he went to the pawn shop and bought him a tenor guitar, four string, to learn it to sit on the band and play. He wanted to be in the band; he didn't want to be off and play the piano on certain things. That was his situation.
